newsitem.title: USA: Susie Maroney nears end of Cuba-to-Florida swim.
newsitem.headline: Susie Maroney nears end of Cuba-to-Florida swim.

text.p: Australian marathon swimmer Susie Maroney, 22, neared her goal of a U.S. landfall on Monday as she passed Sand Key, a tiny island about six miles (10 km) east-southeast of Key West.
"She's going with the tide and with the current," said Connie Tignatiello, one of Maroney's U.S. coordinators, who said she was in contact with Maroney's lead boat, the Reel Lady.
Shortly before 10 a.m. EDT (1400 GMT), Maroney was about one-half mile (0.8 km) from Sand Key. She left Havana at 11:46 a.m. EDT (1546 GMT) on Sunday.
Tignatiello said she expected Maroney to make landfall in between 1-1/2 and three hours.

"She's strong enough to swim right up to Fort Taylor Beach," she said, referring to the historic fort on the western tip of Key West, considered the southernmost point in the continental United States.

Maroney had already bested her failed effort last year to become the first person to cross the 90-mile (145-km) Florida Straits, which divide Florida and Cuba and have been considered one of swimming's last great challenges.

A storm, heavy seas and adverse currents forced Maroney to abandon that attempt last June when she was only 12 miles (19 km) short of the Florida Keys and after she had battled for 38-1/2 hours. She vomited and hallucinated before being plucked from the water.
Two television crews, from Australia and the United States, were aboard accompanying boats, filming Maroney's current attempt.

Tignatiello said one of the pontoons supporting the shark cage had been damaged overnight on Sunday as Maroney swam through rough water, raising questions about how long the swimmer would be able to remain in the cage.
"They're scared to let her out of the shark cage, because not only is it rough but they've spotted two sharks," she said.
